parse.title: Oscar Wilde
parse.text:
Attributed

[edit]
  • I have the simplest tastes. I am always satisfied with the best.
    • Reported in Edgar Saltus, Oscar Wilde: An Idler's Impression (1917), p. 20 [1]
  • God knows; I won't be an Oxford don anyhow. I'll be a poet, a writer, a dramatist. Somehow or other I'll be famous, and if not famous, I'll be notorious. Or perhaps I'll lead the life of pleasure for a time and then—who knows?—rest and do nothing. What does Plato say is the highest end that man can attain here below? To sit down and contemplate the good. Perhaps that will be the end of me too.
    • Reported in Sir David Oswald Hunter-Blair, In Victorian Days and Other Papers (1939), p. 122 [2]
  • If it took Labouchere three columns to prove that I was forgotten, then there is no difference between fame and obscurity.
    • Reported in The New-York Herald (12 August 1883) [3]
  • I think Oscar Wilde said, "Everything in human life is really about sex, except sex. Sex is about power."
    • Michael Cunningham, interview by Paul Lisicky, "A Talk with Michael Cunningham", Provincetown Arts, vol. 11 (1995), p. 39
